factsAccepted: Revenue declined from $850M (FY2023) to $800M (FY2025), a 5.9% decrease, while EBITDA margin fell from 6% to 4% (-200 bps). EBITDA fell from ~$51M to ~$32M (-37%). The margin decline outpaces the revenue decline, indicating fixed costs are not flexing down as the demand base shrinks.

Same-store sales declined approximately 4% per year over the period, indicating demand contraction at the existing footprint rather than a one-time shock. The 45-store base was sized and staffed for a higher demand level that is no longer materializing, leaving stores under-trafficked.

Inventory grew approximately 12% over two years while revenue fell 5.9%, so inventory turnover deteriorated and markdown rates rose. Buying and allocation remained planned to a higher demand forecast than the market delivered, leaving excess seasonal inventory cleared at markdown and compressing gross margin.

E-commerce is only ~14% of the chain's sales versus ~30%+ for stronger department-store peers, while off-price and online competitors (Amazon, Target, TJX) capture the mid-tier shopper. The traditional in-store demand the footprint was forecast against is migrating to channels and competitors the company under-serves.
